title: Former Republican Sen. Jon Kyl of Arizona says he has dementia
summary: Former Republican U.S. Sen. Jon Kyl of Arizona announced his withdrawal from public life following a dementia diagnosis.

title: Democrat wins Iowa special election, keeps GOP from reclaiming supermajority
summary: Following the November 2024 general election, Republicans expanded their majority to 67 out of 100 seats, which meets the two-thirds threshold required for a supermajority. Democrats hold 33 seats.

title: Ben Nighthorse Campbell, former U.S. senator and Native American, dies at 92
summary: Former Sen. Ben Nighthorse Campbell, a Northern Cheyenne tribal chief who became a prominent American politician, has died.

title: Trump issues his first vetoes of this term
summary: President Trump used his veto power this week for the first time since returning to the White House, rejecting a pair of bills linked to a Colorado water pipeline and a tribal village in the Everglades.

title: HHS freezes all child care payments to Minnesota after viral fraud allegations
summary: The Department of Health and Human Services said Tuesday it has frozen federal child care funding for the state of Minnesota, citing viral fraud allegations.

title: Court order suggests officials pushed to prosecute Abrego Garcia after deportation
summary: A court order suggests the Trump administration pushed to prosecute Kilmar Abrego Garcia only after he challenged his deportation, with one top DOJ official calling it a "top priority."

title: ICE can access some Medicaid information for deportation efforts, judge says
summary: U.S. District Court Judge Vince Chhabria said in an order Monday the Department of Homeland Security can receive biographical, contact and location information from the Medicaid program.

title: Dutch angry at U.S. for yanking panels honoring Black World War II troops
summary: The removal by a U.S. military cemetery in the Netherlands of two displays recognizing Black troops who fought in World War II has spurred anger there.

title: D.C. pipe bomb suspect told authorities "something just snapped," DOJ says
summary: Brian Cole told investigators he believed that the 2020 election had been tampered with and he felt "someone needs to speak up," the DOJ alleges in court documents.

title: Trump and Zelenskyy meeting in Florida to talk Ukraine peace plan
summary: President Trump said Sunday that he had a "good and very productive" call with Russian President Vladimir Putin ahead of the meeting with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy.

title: Trump establishing a hard line on foreign policy
summary: During his first year back in power, President Trump has used American military might to send messages to adversaries abroad. On Christmas Day, Mr. Trump ordered a strike on ISIS militants in Nigeria, which came about one week after the U.S. also struck ISIS targets in Syria. Willie James Inman reports from Mar-a-Lago.

title: Russia launches massive attack on Kyiv with drones, missiles ahead of Trump-Zelenskyy meeting
summary: For approximately 10 hours Saturday, Russia attacked the Ukrainian capital city of Kyiv with about 500 drones and 40 missiles. The assault left about one-third of the city without power. The attack comes one day before before Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy meets with President Trump in Mar-a-Lago. Elizabeth Palmer has the latest.

title: Trump calls for release of any Epstein files naming Democrats: "Embarrass them"
summary: As prosecutors contend with a massive trove of Epstein files, President Trump suggested Friday the Justice Department is spending too much time on the issue — but said Democrats should be named.

title: Kennedy Center Christmas Eve concert canceled after Trump's name added
summary: A planned Christmas Eve jazz concert at the Kennedy Center has been canceled.

title: Trump promises to guard against "bad Santa" in Christmas Eve calls with kids
summary: =President Trump spent part of Christmas Eve bantering with kids, updating families on NORAD's Santa tracker and reminding one child that the big guy has a "serious appetite."

title: Poll: Spending time with family is what Americans like most about the holidays

summary: A federal judge gave the Trump administration two weeks to submit a plan to either return a group of men previously held at a notorious Salvadoran prison to the U.S., or give them a hearing to contest allegations of gang membership.

summary: The 2025 Kennedy Center Honors will be broadcast tonight, Dec. 23, celebrating George Strait, Gloria Gaynor, Kiss, Michael Crawford and Sylvester Stallone.

title: Trump calls release of photos of people in Epstein files "a terrible thing"
summary: President Trump has responded to the release of the Epstein files, saying Monday that the release of photos risked ensnaring "highly respected" people with no connection to Epstein's crimes.

title: Blumenthal seeks details on White House ballroom from architect, dinner attendees
summary: Democratic Sen. Richard Blumenthal is pushing for more information on a White House ballroom project championed by President Trump, sending letters to the project's architect and some fundraising dinner attendees.

title: Partial release of Epstein files draws backlash against Trump administration
summary: The Justice Department released more of its files on convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein over the weekend. But the partial release, full of redactions, came after a deadline Congress set for releasing all of the files. Scott MacFarlane has the latest.

title: RFK Jr. says he'll work with agencies to wind down animal testing
summary: Animal rights groups celebrate, but the Trump administration is light on specifics about phasing out federally funded medical testing on animals.

title: Mayor-elect Zohran Mamdani to be sworn in by Letitia James, Bernie Sanders
summary: New York City Mayor-elect Zohran Mamdani​ will be sworn in by two prominent Democrats on New Year's Day.

title: Trump announces new "Trump class" of Navy battleships
summary: President Trump announced plans to build a new "Trump class" of battleships, part of the Pentagon's new "Golden Fleet."

title: Judge orders Kilmar Abrego Garcia to remain free until at least next week
summary: Kilmar Abrego Garcia — who was mistakenly deported to El Salvador in March — will remain free on supervised release until at least the end of the year.

title: Vance tries to unify conservatives as rifts exposed at Turning Point USA
summary: Rifts over the direction of the conservative movement emerged during Turning Point USA's conference, as speakers attacked each other by name.

title: DHS offers undocumented migrants $3,000 if they self-deport by end of 2025
summary: The Department of Homeland Security has tripled its "exit bonus" offered to undocumented migrants who voluntarily leave the United States by Dec. 31, 2025.

summary: More see Trump's policies responsible for economy today than Biden's; there are also concerns about AI impact on jobs.

title: Walz, state officials question federal claim about fraud in Minnesota
summary: Federal prosecutors said the total fraud in Minnesota's Medicaid programs could be as much as $9 billion, but DFL Gov. Tim Walz and other state officials disputed that the amount of taxpayer money stolen is that high.

title: What to know about Minnesota's "industrial-scale fraud" scandal
summary: Federal prosecutors have unveiled charges against six more people accused of defrauding programs in Minnesota — adding to a scandal that has ensnared over 90 people.

title: Minnesota Gov. Walz unveils new fraud prevention program
summary: Democratic Minnesota Gov. Tim Walz on Friday unveiled a new statewide fraud prevention program in the state's latest effort to crack down in the wake of the Feeding Our Future scandal — a scheme that siphoned away $250 million in taxpayer funds meant for hungry children.

title: Potential funding pauses in response to fraud have nonprofits worried
summary: The federal and state crackdowns on fraud in Minnesota are creating collateral damage in programs aimed at helping people with disabilities.

title: Minnesota officials saw signs of massive fraud even before COVID hit
summary: In July 2019, Minnesota state officials spotted early signs of fraud that would eventually siphon away more than $1 billion in taxpayer money, sources told CBS News.

title: Treasury investigating whether Minnesota welfare money went to al Shabaab
summary: The Trump administration is looking into whether Minnesota tax money found its way to al Shabaab, an al Qaeda affiliate based in Somalia, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said.

title: Walz orders third party to audit Medicaid billing at Minnesota DHS
summary: Gov. Tim Walz on Wednesday said that a third party will audit billing for 14 Medicaid services that are deemed to be "high risk" for fraud in Minnesota.
